questions.stem: With which architecture is Kappa Architecture most often confused?
questions.explanation: Kappa is mostly confused with Lambda Architecture, which is fair because both process streaming as well as batch data.

questions.stem: What kind of processing does Kappa Architecture offer?
options: Stream processing only, for both streaming and batch datasets
questions.explanation: Kappa Architecture offers ONLY stream processing, using queuing tools such as Kafka for both streaming and batch datasets.

questions.stem: Which queuing tool is named as the example used by Kappa Architecture?
questions.explanation: Kappa Architecture processes both real-time streaming and batch data using the same tool, with KAFKA given as the example.

questions.stem: What is described as the biggest differentiator of Kappa Architecture from Lambda?
options: It uses a separate tool for batch processing
It is only available in the cloud
It requires an RDBMS for storage
It stores data in a separate data store that might not suit terabytes or petabytes
questions.explanation: Kappa stores data in a separate data store which might not be suitable for TBs or PBs, unlike Lambda which stores in Hadoop or object storage.

options: Due to high demand for real-time data
To reduce the cost of Hadoop clusters
questions.explanation: Kappa Architecture emerged due to the high demand for real-time data, though not for all data sizes.

questions.stem: Which organisation should choose Lambda rather than Kappa Architecture?
options: One with small data and no history requirement
One with terabytes or potentially petabytes of data
One that only needs a message queue
One that uses only on-premises servers
One that has no real-time requirement at all
questions.explanation: Organisations with TBs or PBs of data should go for Lambda Architecture and store data in Hadoop or object storage for analysis.

questions.stem: For which situation is Kappa Architecture recommended?
options: Small or medium-sized data with no historical data maintenance requirement
questions.explanation: Kappa suits small or medium data volumes where there is no requirement to maintain historical data.

questions.stem: How do batch-related downstream applications get their data in Kappa Architecture?
options: By connecting directly to Kappa's storage
questions.explanation: Kappa Architecture offers batch-related downstream applications the ability to connect directly to its storage.

questions.stem: Where does Lambda Architecture store data for analysis and analytics, in contrast to Kappa?
questions.explanation: With Lambda, data is stored in Hadoop or object storage for analysis and analytics, which suits very large volumes.

questions.stem: Which statement about Kappa Architecture is FALSE?
options: It processes both streaming and batch data
It uses a single tool such as Kafka for both
It provides separate tools and technologies to process batches
It is not suitable for all data sizes
It emerged from the demand for real-time data
questions.explanation: Kappa does not offer separate tools or technologies to process batches; everything is handled as a stream by the same tool.
